matches.rationale: Finding 5 directly identifies that the Abstract claims a d^{O(1/ε)} rate for simplex ℓ1 calibration while the paper's own Corollary C.5 yields d^{O(1/ε^2)}. This is the same inflated sample complexity described in GT 1.

Finding 6 points out that the Abstract says the lower bound proves T≥exp(Ω(1/ε)) and implies tightness, but the actual Theorem 4.3 only gives exp(Ω(ε^{-1/6})). This matches the exaggeration of the lower bound and false suggestion of tightness described in GT 2.
No finding mentions the fabricated citation [ZKL23] or the missing reference in the bibliography. The corruption is not detected by any finding.

Finding 1 identifies that Section 2.3 defines the Bregman divergence with reversed arguments (D_R(y||p)=R(p)-R(y)-⟨∇R(y),p-y⟩) while subsequent lemmas silently use the correct form. This is the exact definitional reversal and its logical consequence described in GT 4.
No finding addresses the claim that TreeCal does not require knowledge of ρ despite the proof using ρ to set parameters. This implementation misrepresentation is not raised.
No finding discusses the contradictory statements that TreeCal is nearly identical to prior work yet the analysis is novel. The framing incoherence is not mentioned.
No finding mentions the misleading 'bound is independent of d' claim for ℓ2 calibration while the diameter term depends on d. This overstatement is not detected.
Although strong convexity is used throughout, no finding identifies an error in its definition (whether it is ≥ or ≤). The corruption to the strong convexity inequality is undetected.
No finding mentions the rhetorical overstatement that the work 'completely solves' the problem. The exaggeration is not flagged.
No finding points out the altered constant from 3 to 1 in Theorem C.1. The tightening of the swap regret bound is not noted.
No finding discusses the absence of a funding acknowledgment or conflict-of-interest disclosure for the Google Research authors. The omission is not raised.
No finding notes the logical inconsistency that BTL is called unimplementable yet its regret is used as a benchmark. This contradiction is not detected.
No finding identifies the confusion over whether TreeSwap is novel or prior art, or the misattribution of the analysis. The inconsistency is not mentioned.

Finding 3 reports that Claim C.3 is printed with a reversed inequality (≥ instead of ≤), which would break the proof and invalidate the calibration bound. This matches the sign-reversal corruption described in GT 14.
No finding mentions the missing centrally symmetric requirement for the claim that the results hold for an arbitrary convex set and arbitrary norm. The overstatement is not caught.
No finding discusses the absence of a computational complexity analysis despite the claim that TreeCal is 'highly efficient'. The omission is not detected.

Finding 2 identifies that the calibration error definition in Section 2.1 uses a 1/T factor (making it normalized) while FullSwapReg and subsequent theorems use unnormalized quantities. This is the same normalization corruption described in GT 17.

Finding 7 notes the exponent inconsistency in the lower bound: Section 4 states d^{1/7} while the introduction and the underlying proof support d^{1/14}. This exactly matches the fabrication of a weaker exponent described in GT 18.
